organization_name: VA Disability Claim Denial -- AMA Three-Lane Appeal System
statutory_authority: Appeals Modernization Act (Pub. L. 115-55, 2017) | 38 U.S.C. sec. 5104C | 38 CFR Part 3, Part 20

appeal_deadline.text: 1 YEAR from the date printed on the VA decision letter -- calendar days, not business days -- to file in ANY of the three lanes and preserve your original effective date

continued_benefits_deadline.text: Not generally applicable to initial disability compensation claims -- there is no ongoing benefit to "continue" until the claim is granted. (See separate entry for reduction of an existing rating, where continuation protections differ.)

hearing_request_deadline.text: For Board Appeal Hearing docket: request at time of filing VA Form 10182, within the 1-year deadline

reconsideration_deadline.text: Not a separate step under AMA -- Higher-Level Review functions as the reconsideration-equivalent lane

judicial_review_deadline.text: 120 days from a Board of Veterans Appeals decision to appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC)

notes: The 1-year deadline runs from the date ON THE LETTER, not the date received -- calendar the deadline the day you get any decision letter. Missing it does not end your ability to ever claim again, but you lose the original effective date and years of potential retroactive back pay. Choosing the wrong lane is the most common costly mistake -- match the lane to whether you have NEW evidence (Supplemental Claim) or believe the SAME evidence was misread (Higher-Level Review).

organization_name: Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC) -- Final Judicial Review
statutory_authority: 38 U.S.C. sec. 7252 (CAVC jurisdiction) | 38 U.S.C. sec. 7266 (notice of appeal, 120-day deadline)

appeal_deadline.text: Not applicable at this stage -- this entry IS the appeal from the Board decision

hearing_request_deadline.text: Not applicable -- CAVC proceedings are conducted on briefs, not hearings, in the vast majority of cases

reconsideration_deadline.text: CAVC has its own motion for reconsideration process -- typically 21 days from the CAVC decision, verify current court rule

judicial_review_deadline.text: 120 days from the Board of Veterans Appeals decision to file Notice of Appeal with CAVC

notes: 120-day deadline is calculated from the date of the Board decision, not the date you receive it -- confirm the exact date on your Board decision notice. A remand is a partial win, not a loss -- it means the legal or factual error you identified was recognized.

organization_name: Discharge Upgrade -- Discharge Review Board (Under 15 Years)
statutory_authority: 10 U.S.C. sec. 1553 (discharge review boards) | DoD Instruction 1332.28 | Kurta Memo (2017) | Wilkie Memo (2018)

appeal_deadline.text: 15 YEARS from the date of separation to apply to the Discharge Review Board -- after this, only the Board for Correction of Military Records (BCMR/BCNR) can review the case, under different and generally stricter rules

hearing_request_deadline.text: Request an in-person hearing at time of filing DD Form 293, before the 15-year deadline

reconsideration_deadline.text: Each service branch sets its own reconsideration policy for DRB decisions -- verify with the specific branch's review board

judicial_review_deadline.text: Federal court review of DRB decisions is available but rare and highly fact-specific -- consult a veterans' or military law attorney

notes: Start as soon as possible -- as the 15-year deadline approaches, only the stricter BCMR process remains available. If your discharge involved PTSD, military sexual trauma, or TBI-related misconduct, explicitly cite the Kurta and Wilkie memos requiring liberal consideration of mental-health-related circumstances.

organization_name: Discharge Upgrade -- Board for Correction of Military Records (Any Age, Including Over 15 Years)
official_contact: Army (ARBA): 703-571-0141 | Air Force: 240-612-5502 | Navy/Marine Corps (BCNR): 202-685-6600 | Coast Guard: 202-795-6763
statutory_authority: 10 U.S.C. sec. 1552 (correction of military records) | DD Form 149

appeal_deadline.text: No fixed outer deadline to APPLY to the BCMR itself, but you must apply within 3 YEARS of discovering the error or injustice you are asking the Board to correct

hearing_request_deadline.text: Hearings are rare and granted at Board discretion -- request explicitly in your DD Form 149 submission

reconsideration_deadline.text: Each branch sets its own reconsideration policy for BCMR/BCNR decisions -- verify with the specific board

judicial_review_deadline.text: Federal court review (typically Court of Federal Claims or U.S. District Court) is available but specialized -- consult a military law attorney

notes: The 3-year clock runs from DISCOVERY of the error, not from separation -- if you only recently learned that PTSD or MST contributed to your discharge characterization, that recent discovery can support a timely application even decades after separation. The Board CAN waive the 3-year deadline "in the interest of justice" -- homelessness, economic hardship, PTSD, and lack of awareness of eligibility have all been argued successfully as grounds for waiver.

organization_name: PACT Act -- Toxic Exposure Presumptive Conditions

appeal_deadline.text: Standard 1-year AMA appeal deadline applies if a PACT Act presumptive claim is denied (see AMA entry above)

continued_benefits_deadline.text: Not applicable to new PACT Act claims

hearing_request_deadline.text: Not applicable at the initial claim stage

reconsideration_deadline.text: Not applicable -- use Higher-Level Review or Supplemental Claim lanes if denied

judicial_review_deadline.text: 120 days from Board decision to CAVC, same as standard AMA appeals (see CAVC entry above)

notes: File an Intent to File immediately, even before you are ready to submit a complete claim -- this locks in your effective date and can mean the difference between one year and zero years of retroactive back pay. The presumptive-condition list has continued to expand through 2025-2026 -- a condition denied in the past may now qualify; consider a Supplemental Claim if you were previously denied for a condition now on the presumptive list.

organization_name: VA Disability Rating Reduction -- Due Process Protections
statutory_authority: 38 CFR sec. 3.105(e) (reduction procedures) | 38 CFR sec. 3.344 (stabilized ratings)

appeal_deadline.text: Standard 1-year AMA deadline applies once the reduction decision is actually issued

continued_benefits_deadline.text: Submit evidence and/or request a hearing within 60 days of the PROPOSED reduction notice -- doing so preserves your current rating unchanged until the final decision is issued

hearing_request_deadline.text: Within 60 days of the proposed reduction notice, alongside or instead of submitting evidence

reconsideration_deadline.text: Not a separate step -- use the 60-day pre-reduction response window, then AMA lanes if reduction proceeds

judicial_review_deadline.text: 120 days from Board decision to CAVC if the reduction is upheld through the full appeal process

notes: The 60-day response window to a PROPOSED reduction is the single most important deadline in this entry -- responding within it keeps your current rating unchanged while the VA considers your evidence. This is functionally the VA equivalent of a "continued benefits" protection and should not be confused with the 1-year AMA appeal deadline that applies only after a final reduction decision is issued.

organization_name: VA Office of Inspector General -- Reporting VA Misconduct and Malpractice
statutory_authority: Inspector General Act of 1978 (5 U.S.C. App. 3) | 38 U.S.C. sec. 312

appeal_deadline.text: Not applicable -- this is a reporting/investigative mechanism, not an appeal

judicial_review_deadline.text: Not applicable -- for malpractice claims resulting in injury, see the separate FTCA entry below

notes: OIG does not handle benefits appeals -- redirect anyone with a claim denial to the AMA lanes instead. For urgent safety issues, use the facility Patient Advocate in parallel with an OIG report, since the Patient Advocate can act faster.

organization_name: VA Medical Malpractice -- Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) Process
official_contact: Contact VA Regional Counsel where the malpractice occurred | VA main line: 800-827-1000
statutory_authority: Federal Tort Claims Act (28 U.S.C. sec. 2671 et seq.) | 38 U.S.C. sec. 1151 (benefits for VA-caused injury)

appeal_deadline.text: Not applicable in the AMA sense -- see specific FTCA and Section 1151 deadlines below

hearing_request_deadline.text: Not applicable to the administrative claim stage

reconsideration_deadline.text: Not applicable -- if VA denies the SF-95, the next step is federal court, not administrative reconsideration

judicial_review_deadline.text: File SF-95 within 2 years of the malpractice (or discovery of injury). If VA denies or does not respond within 6 months, file suit in U.S. District Court within 6 months of the denial notice.

notes: FTCA malpractice claims and Section 1151 benefits claims are separate tracks that can be pursued simultaneously -- do not assume filing one forecloses the other. The mandatory administrative claim (SF-95) before suing is frequently misunderstood; skipping straight to federal court without first filing the SF-95 will get the case dismissed.
